notes: Wiring follows the circuit image and the pin table: ST->A0, Z->A1, Y->A2, X->A3, GND->A4, VDD->A5. A4 is driven LOW as ground and A5 HIGH as 5V in code. The schematic crosses X/Z, but the image and table are taken as authoritative.

The breakout's 6-pin header sits in breadboard columns 4-9 at the row nearest the top of the image (labelled j in the image). The catalogue's top bank 't' is rows a-e, so I used 't' holes: module in row e, wires in row d of the same columns. Any hole in the same column-bank is the same strip, so the connectivity is unchanged.
The Arduino is assumed to be powered over USB, which the manual does not show, so no USB cable is included.
The ADXL335 catalogue type stands in for the generic ADXL3xx breakout. Its ports are ST, Z, Y, X, GND, VCC, and VDD on the board is mapped to VCC.
The MCP connectors (Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Drive) need authorization, but they were not used for this task.
